Applied.Outcome: Applied: AWS and Azure compared in the text. AWS cannot issue a publicly trusted code-signing certificate (Certificate Manager is TLS only, Private CA is not trusted by Windows, Signer needs an importable key the CAs no longer give); it can only hold a KMS key for a certificate bought elsewhere ($200 to $600 a year) signed through Jsign. Azure Trusted Signing is the CA itself at $9.99 a month, supported natively by electron-builder. Decided: Azure Trusted Signing, with the setup steps listed.

Replies.Text: i currently use AWS as a primary cloud provider. Compare certificate services from both AWS and Azure.

Replies.Text:
Build log: the icon (Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14).

What was built:
- The branding image is the mark the docs already had (docs/images/mark.svg: the open ring with a check, in the accent color). No new drawing; the speech-bubble proposal is dropped from the text. The master copy is public/img/mark.svg, served by the web server and the desktop.
- desktop/icon.ico (16 to 256 pixels) and desktop/icon.png (512) rendered from the master with ImageMagick; the command lines are in the plan so it can be redone. package.json names the .ico in win.icon.
- public/index.html links the SVG as the favicon in place of the empty data URL, and the About popup shows the mark before its title; one rule, .about-mark, in consensus.css.
- No .icns: this ImageMagick cannot write one; it comes with the Mac build.

How it was tested:
- npm run dist rebuilt the installer with no icon warning; the icon extracted from the built Consensus.exe and from Consensus Setup 0.4.0.exe is the mark.
- The running server serves /img/mark.svg as image/svg+xml and the page carries the favicon link and the About mark.
- npm test: 179 pass, 0 fail.

Not committed. The plan stays Working until this log is resolved; then one commit, "Installer: the icon".
